name: GitCompete
description: GitCompete compares two public GitHub profiles with an intentionally visible scoring formula.

paragraphs: GitCompete compares two public GitHub profiles with an intentionally visible scoring formula. It is a small frontend showcase built around a real external API, loading/error states, responsive layout, accessible controls, theme persistence, and shareable comparison URLs.

The original project put a GitHub OAuth secret in browser code and depended on an obsolete Webpack/React stack. This version uses GitHub's unauthenticated public endpoints instead. That keeps the application deployable as a static site and, most importantly, means there is no browser-exposed secret to protect. A server-side token can be added later only if real users hit the public rate limit often enough to justify owning that operational responsibility.

whatItDoes.text: GitCompete compares two public GitHub profiles with an intentionally visible scoring formula. It is a small frontend showcase built around a real external API, loading/error states, responsive layout, accessible controls, theme persistence, and shareable comparison URLs.

requirements.text: Uses the public GitHub REST API directly—no sign-in, backend, secret, or client ID required.
